tone: Clear, concise, friendly US software language; avoid slang and marketing hype.
capitalization: Use sentence case for labels and headings unless a proper name requires capitals.
button_labels: Use short imperative verbs and omit terminal punctuation.
ui_roles: Keep labels concise, buttons action-oriented, tooltips explanatory, warnings direct, and errors complete natural sentences.
technical_terms: Follow the approved glossary and preserve every protected token verbatim.
contextual_terminology: Choose each ambiguous term from its stable ID, feature context, surface type, and neighboring strings; do not enforce one global wording.
punctuation: Use US punctuation and quotation conventions; preserve required accelerators.
units: Preserve numeric meaning; use established US UI formatting only when context requests it.
natural_language: Prefer idiomatic, direct wording over literal or source-order phrasing.
